label: Game B
nuance_found: One tide dial does everything but each job wants a different level and timing: pull the sea down to cross the causeway, raise it to fill the well and lift the bucket, hold it high to float Tam's boat, keep it inside a moving bright band to thread the Needles (too low hits reefs, too high hits the arch), and for the crab boss lure it with high water, strand it by dropping the sea slowly, then slam the sea back fast and hit Shine. Letting go lets the sea drift home, so holding a level is itself a decision. Side requests (Pip's toy boat, Marta's pots) reuse the same dial in a different way.
audio: Soft ambient wind drone from the start, a harbour tune that comes in after about 20 s, little chimes and sliding tones when something changes, a bright chord on pickups; pleasant, but quiet and sparse compared with a Royal Match.
furthest_progress: Finished the main story: Nell, well shard, Tam's boat, Shellflats wreck lens, Needles with 5 knocks, beat the Undertow crab (3 of 3), lit the Stack lighthouse at about 300 s; end card '5 min on the coast, 67 m of sea moved, 5 knocks, 0 of 5 lost things found'. Second run: started Pip's toy boat and Marta's pots quests, got the boat to the beach, found 0 of 5 lost things.
control_trouble: Walking was done almost entirely by the assist. Fast drags on the tide lantern were ignored (needed slow drags of 1 to 1.5 s), and the needle band and crab timing are hard with a 0.5 s view; a real thumb would be smoother. After the ending, the assist said no route to most places, so free roam was hard to judge.
best_moment: Raising the sea under the wreck so the raft floats up to the cabin, then sailing the Needles with the arch sliding overhead.
worst_moment: The first minute is tapping through four lines of Nell talking before I touch anything, and after the lighthouse the game just ends with no clear next thing and a dark, empty world.
verdict: This one is gorgeous, a little storybook you play with one finger, and the sea-going-up-and-down idea is a new trick every minute or so: cross the causeway, float the raft, thread the stone arches, trap a giant crab. I always knew what to do next because the top card told me. But it is a slow walk, there is lots of reading, and there are no frequent little wins like in my usual games. The whole thing was over in about five minutes, with a nice ending, and then there is not much to chase except a few lost items I could not find. I would tell a friend to try it once on the bus, but I do not know that I would come back tomorrow.
